candidate.title: 3’-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina poster row “3’-Seq to detect 3’UTR isoforms”, interpreted as the bead-associated, uridine-directed nick-translation implementation described by Lianoglou et al. (2013). 3′-Seq/3′-seq are typographic renderings of this target. The neighboring 3P-Seq, 2P-seq, and TIF-Seq rows and the right-hand chemical legend are context, with no connecting arrows or depicted alternatives within the assigned row. The matching collection page 17 is secondary catalogue evidence. The architecture ends at the depicted cDNA library; readout interpretation is explained without adding unshown sequencing-analysis operations. The primary source resolves the omitted second-adapter interface. No historical development or equivalence to other end-sequencing assays is asserted.

states.label: Purified, PCR-amplified cDNA library representing RNA 3′ ends
features: The poster endpoint is a single blue line labeled cDNA. At the primary-supported implementation level, it represents an amplified double-stranded DNA sequencing library, not the original RNA or a requirement for a single-stranded final product.

Transcript-derived 3′ tags carry the association between a sequenced DNA insert and a polyadenylated RNA end; mapping and counting such tags can identify cleavage/polyadenylation sites and quantify relative 3′ UTR isoform abundance.
This is an end-tag readout; it does not pair the original 5′ and 3′ ends or reconstruct full-length transcript molecules.
Oligo(dT) priming does not guarantee authentic poly(A)-end specificity: the primary study removes internal-priming peaks. No analysis thresholds are part of this graph.
The final product is drawn without a bead. PCR generates library copies from the bead-associated template; no separate chemical detachment step is asserted.
